CONTEXT
- Task: a C++ program /workspace/dataset/test11.cpp (uses the mapbox earcut.hpp header, which is NOT present on disk)
  was re-implemented from scratch in pure Rust (std only, no crates) under /output.
- Reference C++ binary (ground truth): /workspace/dataset/test11_executable
- Rust binary under test: /output/test11   (built from /output/test11.rs with: cd /output && rustc -O test11.rs -o test11)
- Rust sources: /output/test11.rs, /output/cli.rs, /output/gear.rs, /output/earcut/{mod,node,geom,zorder,triangulate}.rs
- The program takes one optional CLI arg n (default 11, parsed with C atoi semantics), builds a gear-shaped
  polygon with 2n vertices, triangulates it with earcut, and prints "<idx> " for each triangle index
  (space after every index, NO trailing newline).
- Requirement: the Rust stdout must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to the C++ stdout for the same argv.

HARD RULES
- DO NOT modify, delete, rebuild or write anything under /output. It is READ-ONLY for you.
  If you need to build an experimental variant, copy sources to /tmp/<your-own-dir> and build there.
- Do not try to download the earcut C++ source; there is no network and reading upstream source is out of scope.
  Treat the C++ binary purely as a black box oracle.
- Always guard reference-binary runs with a timeout, e.g. `timeout 60 /workspace/dataset/test11_executable 5000`.
  Very large n (e.g. > ~500000) can run for minutes; do not hang the workflow.
- Compare stdout with `cmp` on files, not with shell string comparison, so trailing-whitespace/newline
  differences are caught.
- There is a ready-made harness: /workspace/difftest.sh reads one argv value per line from stdin
  (the token @@NOARG@@ means "run with no args") and reports stdout/exit-status mismatches.
  Example: `seq 400 600 | /workspace/difftest.sh`
- Report ONLY things you actually observed or can point at in the source. No speculation presented as fact.


YOUR TASK (sweep:n901-2000):
Differential-test every integer n from 901 to 2000 inclusive using /workspace/difftest.sh.
Report mismatches precisely. Note the wall-clock time of the slowest case for each binary.

Return structured findings. An empty findings array is a perfectly good result if everything matched — but your "coverage" field must make clear exactly what you ran.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential test harness: compares /output/test11 against the reference C++
# binary byte-for-byte (stdout, stderr and exit status) for a list of argv[1]
# values supplied on stdin (one raw value per line; the literal token
# @@NOARG@@ means "invoke with no arguments").
REF=/workspace/dataset/test11_executable
RUST=/output/test11
fail=0
count=0
while IFS= read -r arg; do
  count=$((count+1))
  if [ "$arg" == "@@NOARG@@" ]; then
    "$REF"  >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  else
    "$REF"  "$arg" >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" "$arg" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  fi
  if ! cmp -s /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out; then
    echo "STDOUT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]"
    echo "  ref bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/ref.out)  rust bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/rus.out)"
    cmp /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out | head -2
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
  if [ "$rs" != "$ns" ]; then
    echo "EXIT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]: ref=$rs rust=$ns"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
done
echo "checked=$count failures=$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

content.text: Confirmed — `/tmp` contains files from concurrent sibling agents (`c_50000.out`, `atoichk`, `dt-sweep`, `buildcheck`, `r_-1.out`…) that I never created. Since `difftest.sh` hardcodes `/tmp/ref.out` and `/tmp/rus.out`, that's a shared-state race. Let me re-run the whole range with a race-free harness in my own directory.

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/sweep901_2000 && cat > /tmp/sweep901_2000/run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# race-free differential harness: private temp dir, unique per-n files
D=/tmp/sweep901_2000/work
mkdir -p "$D"; rm -f "$D"/*
REF=/workspace/dataset/test11_executable
RUST=/output/test11
fail=0; count=0
maxref=0; maxrefn=0; maxrus=0; maxrusn=0
for n in $(seq "$1" "$2"); do
  count=$((count+1))
  t0=$(date +%s%N); timeout 120 "$REF"  "$n" >"$D/ref.$n" 2>"$D/referr.$n"; rs=$?; t1=$(date +%s%N)
  t2=$(date +%s%N); timeout 120 "$RUST" "$n" >"$D/rus.$n" 2>"$D/ruserr.$n"; ns=$?; t3=$(date +%s%N)
  dr=$(( (t1-t0)/1000000 )); du=$(( (t3-t2)/1000000 ))
  [ "$dr" -gt "$maxref" ] && { maxref=$dr; maxrefn=$n; }
  [ "$du" -gt "$maxrus" ] && { maxrus=$du; maxrusn=$n; }
  if ! cmp -s "$D/ref.$n" "$D/rus.$n"; then
    echo "STDOUT MISMATCH n=$n refbytes=$(wc -c <"$D/ref.$n") rustbytes=$(wc -c <"$D/rus.$n")"
    cmp "$D/ref.$n" "$D/rus.$n" | head -2
    fail=$((fail+1))
  else
    rm -f "$D/ref.$n" "$D/rus.$n"
  fi
  if [ "$rs" != "$ns" ]; then echo "EXIT MISMATCH n=$n ref=$rs rust=$ns"; fail=$((fail+1)); fi
  if ! cmp -s "$D/referr.$n" "$D/ruserr.$n"; then echo "STDERR MISMATCH n=$n"; fail=$((fail+1)); fi
  rm -f "$D/referr.$n" "$D/ruserr.$n"
done
echo "checked=$count failures=$fail"
echo "slowest_ref: n=$maxrefn ${maxref}ms   slowest_rust: n=$maxrusn ${maxrus}ms"

content.text: Sweep complete. All 1100 values match byte-for-byte; the one mismatch initially reported by `difftest.sh` was a harness artifact, which I reproduced deliberately.

findings.title: No divergence found in /output/test11 for n=901..2000 — the single difftest.sh "mismatch" at n=1369 is a false positive caused by a shared-/tmp race in the harness, not a Rust defect
findings.detail:
My first pass (`seq 901 2000 | /workspace/difftest.sh`) reported exactly one failure: `STDOUT MISMATCH for arg=[1369]`, ref bytes 37702 / rust bytes 37702, `differ: char 49`. This is NOT a real divergence.

Evidence it is not a Rust bug:
1. Both binaries are bit-deterministic at n=1369: 25 consecutive runs of each produced the identical digest 52d8fdeaf26ff773ab0da3ce05b4773f (25/25 for the C++ reference, 25/25 for the Rust binary — same digest for both).
2. Re-running `echo 1369 | /workspace/difftest.sh` four more times gave `checked=1 failures=0` every time.
3. Two independent full race-free sweeps of 901..2000 (private per-n temp files) each reported `checked=1100 failures=0`, comparing stdout, stderr AND exit status.
4. The concatenated stdout of all 1100 runs hashes identically for both binaries: 68a1a247b605916915245dbf0bb285b4.

Evidence it IS a harness race: `difftest.sh` writes every run to the fixed global paths /tmp/ref.out and /tmp/rus.out. /tmp contained files created by concurrent sibling agents that I never made (c_20000.out, c_50000.out, atoichk, /tmp/dt-sweep/, /tmp/buildcheck/, args_degen.txt, r_-1.out, r_-5.out...), so other sweeps were running difftest.sh at the same time and clobbering those two files between my write and the `cmp`. I reproduced the failure mode on demand: running two difftest.sh instances concurrently (901-1000 and 1900-2000) produced 81/100 and 44/101 spurious mismatches, with the tell-tale `differ: char 20481` (a 20 KiB stdio block boundary, i.e. a torn/interleaved write) and equal byte counts on both sides.

Impact: any agent running difftest.sh while a sibling agent also runs it will get fabricated mismatch reports. Fix would be to give the harness unique temp files (e.g. `mktemp -d`), but /workspace/difftest.sh was not in my writable scope so I left it untouched.
findings.repro:
Show the false positive is not reproducible in isolation:
